review_items.review_title: One of the best NITs in India (MNIT Jaipur)

aspect_evidence.evidence_summary: 'Our batch placement rate is around 89-91 percent. The highest package is 27 LPA. The lowest is around 6 LPA, and the average package is 10 LPA. Top recruiting companies include Honda, HPCL, BPCL, Maruti Suzuki, and ICICI Bank.'
'The on-campus internship rate is quite low.'

'We have the biggest lecture hall in Asia (VLTC). There is a computer centre open 24/7. We also have a workshop that includes different shops like a foundry and a welding shop. Wi-Fi is available across the entire campus. There are different grounds for each sport, both indoor and outdoor.'
'The teaching is very much research-oriented. Some learnings are directly related to the industry.'

'Companies like MediaTek, Micron, Apple, Samsung, Airtel, Qualcomm, Texas Instruments, NVIDIA, and others visit MNIT Jaipur for recruitment. Hence, the highest package ranges between 36.2 and 52 CTC. The minimum salary ranges between 6 and 9 CTC. The average salary ranges between 14 and 18 CTC. Strong placement statistics of around 85-90%, and the internship rate is around 70-80% in local companies and semiconductor production companies. Top job roles offered to ECE students include VLSI engineer, embedded system designer, and ASIC designer.'
'All the academic buildings were in the finest condition with a 50 Mbps Wi-Fi facility all over the campus.'
'MNIT is located in the main city, so you remain connected with the city. For fun or shopping, World Trade Park and Gaurav Tower are also near the campus.'

review_items.review_title: How is ragging at MNIT Jaipur?
review_items.extraction_note: This answer is EXPLICITLY HISTORICAL, describing the institute under its former name (MREC — Malaviya Regional Engineering College) in the 1990s, before its NIT conversion in 2002. This is a meaningfully different era and even a formally different-named institution predecessor. The answer itself contrasts this with 'recent passouts' describing a different present-day experience, which is corroborated by other present-day sources in this dataset describing no ragging. Preserved with full temporal context rather than treated as describing current MNIT Jaipur conditions.

aspect_evidence.evidence_summary: 'MREC as it was called was a terror once upon a time when I studied there in the 1990s. Ragging was sooo severe that we freshers were housed in a separate dormitory for 6-12 months. Ragging was physical often and much more for stud[ents...]' (sentence truncated in retrieved snippet). Answerer explicitly contrasts this with 'the answers from recent passouts,' implying awareness that conditions have since changed.
